extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes the substantive changes and updated guidance in the MPEP (Revision 07.2022) affecting patent prosecution and international (PCT) practice, including duties of disclosure, sequence listing rules, prior art/obviousness analysis, enablement, claim drafting, and procedural/form updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing Nucleotide and/or Amino Acid Sequence Listings in International Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised title to 'Filing Nucleotide and/or Amino Acid Sequence Listings in International Applications.' Added Editor Note clarifying reproduced PCT Rules and Administrative Instructions apply to applications having an international filing date on or after July 1, 2022 and provided a reference to the previous version. In subsection I, revised to incorporate guidance from ST.26 rulemaking. In subsection II, clarified guidance for international applications having an international filing date before July 1, 2022, disclosing sequences (WIPO ST.25). Deleted subsection III because tables related to sequence listings are no longer allowed in PCT international applications. In subsection I, deleted the statement that sequence listings may be filed in ASCII text format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key effects: ST.26-based formatting and submission rules apply for apps on/after July 1, 2022; tables are no longer allowed in PCT international apps; earlier WIPO ST.25 guidance retained for earlier filing dates; updated reproduction of PCT Rule 5.2, Rule 13ter, and Administrative Instructions (including AI 204, AI 208). Guidance also clarifies when an English translation of a sequence listing is required and procedures for the IPEA/US to invite an applicant to furnish a sequence listing and pay a late furnishing fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT procedural and form updates (fees, restoration of priority, corrections, refunds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated reproduction of multiple PCT Rules and Administrative Instructions (e.g., PCT Administrative Instruction 204, PCT Rule 5.2, PCT Rule 13ter, PCT Administrative Instruction 208, PCT Administrative Instruction 513, PCT Rule 71.1). Replaced phrasing to clarify standards used by the International Bureau when deciding requests for restoration of the right of priority (replaced 'has indicated that it intends to decide' with 'decides'). Added a new paragraph setting forth the process for correcting or adding an indication referred to in PCT Rule 4.11. Updated the circumstances when the international and search fees will be refunded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms and sample documents (e.g., PCT/ISA/210, PCT/ISA/237, PCT/IPEA/408, PCT/IPEA/409) were updated. Editorial corrections to form names and paragraphs, clarification of when delays in meeting PCT time limits may be excused or extended, and added cross-references to prior versions for apps with international filing dates before July 1, 2022.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Searching/Preliminary Examining Authority (ISA/IPEA) updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Added Saint Kitts and Nevis to the list of countries for which the USPTO agreed to conduct international searches and prepare international search reports and written opinions. Added Saint Kitts and Nevis to the list where the IPEA/US will serve as International Preliminary Examining Authority for residents or nationals thereof. Clarified that no protest fee under PCT Rule 40.2(e) is due in the ISA/US and that 'The IPEA/US does not charge a protest fee under PCT Rule 68.3(e).' Added guidance that the IPEA may invite the applicant to furnish a sequence listing and pay a late furnishing fee when required. Added 'CPC' to classifications that should be given on Form PCT/IPEA/408 and updated instructions for completing Box IV subsection 1 of that form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updated processing guidance for amendments under PCT Rule 66.8 and Articles 19 and 34, updated sample International Search Report and written opinion forms, and updated instructions for IPEA/US procedures including indexing/classification and amendment periods when entering the U.S. national stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of Disclosure and Reasonable Inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Changed title from 'Reserved' to 'Duty of Disclosure'. Added discussion of Duties of Disclosure and Reasonable Inquiry During Examination, Reexamination, and Reissue, and for Proceedings Before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board. Added that the duty to disclose material information covers all periods 'before the application is granted.' Revised to clarify that presentation to the Office (whether by signing, filing, or submitting) of any paper constitutes a certification which calls for a duty of reasonable inquiry to ensure the paper is not presented for an improper purpose, the legal contentions are warranted by law, factual contentions have evidentiary support, and denials of factual contentions are warranted on the evidence. Revised to emphasize that any material information should be submitted to the Office as early as possible in prosecution or proceedings before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added citations and case references (e.g., Belcher Pharms., GS Cleantech Corp.) and specific suggestions and items clarifying practitioner responsibilities. Emphasized misrepresentations also can occur in declarations; added guidance on distinguishing actual results from predicted results when drafting; duty extends to dealings with other government agencies and documentation submitted to regulatory review bodies may be material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to disclose information inconsistent with applicant positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised to emphasize that applicants should disclose to the USPTO any information that refutes, or is inconsistent with, a position the applicant takes in: (i) opposing an argument of unpatentability relied on by the Office, or (ii) asserting an argument of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item-level revisions (e.g., item 11 changed to 'it is desirable to submit material information') and added item 19 discussing that documentation submitted to a regulatory review body may be relevant to ongoing patent prosecution. Applicants must take care in declarations and in distinguishing actual versus prophetic examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor/natural person requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Added new subsection VII for guidance that an inventor or joint inventor must be a natural person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that corporate or non-natural entities cannot be named as inventors; the updated guidance includes citation additions and aligns definitions with AIA where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obviousness analysis and examiner burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified that the examiner bears the initial burden using facts and reasoning to establish obviousness and that the applicant is under no obligation to submit evidence or arguments to show nonobviousness if the examiner does not produce a prima facie case. Replaced 'time of the invention'/'date of invention' with 'relevant time' throughout obviousness guidance. Clarified that each application must be analyzed on its own facts, considering factual inquiries and secondary considerations when present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added examples of rationales (revised heading to 'Examples of Rationales'), citations to KSR and other Federal Circuit decisions, and cross-references. The guidance emphasizes weighing all relevant evidence, and includes multiple illustrative examples and corrections to citations; KSR-related text was integrated where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102 prior art and exceptions guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified 'effective filing date' by adding 'of a claimed invention.' Clarified that potential references 'within the one-year grace period' are excepted as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(A) and (B). Revised text to better align with statutory text of 35 U.S.C. 102 (e.g., using 'except' rather than 'disqualify'). Added guidance that the subject matter of the prior disclosure relied upon must be the same 'subject matter' as the inventor-originated disclosure for exceptions to apply. Added statements that 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(A)/(B)/(C) exceptions may apply without grace-period limitation in some contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines 'inventor-originated disclosure' (disclosure by an inventor or joint inventor, or another who obtained directly or indirectly from the inventor). Clarifies when affidavits or declarations may be used to except a disclosure, includes illustrative examples (1–4) based on First Inventor to File Declarations training material, and explains effects on double patenting rejections when exceptions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace period extension under 35 U.S.C. 21(b) and electronic filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified when the 1-year grace period is extended under 35 U.S.C. 21(b) notwithstanding provisions of 37 CFR 1.10 and the Office electronic filing system that allow filings during weekends or holidays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarification appears across multiple sections; guidance notes how effective filing deadlines are interpreted in light of electronic filing system timing and statutory grace period extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working and prophetic examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Added that claims should be drafted in a manner that assists readers in differentiating between actual working and prophetic examples. Added new subsection IV to provide guidance on prophetic examples and added 'in art areas having a high degree of uncertainty (i.e. the unpredictable arts)' and guidance on the applicable evidentiary standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated that evaluation of prophetic examples is 'based on a preponderance of evidence standard.' Added citations and discussions (e.g., Pac. Biosciences of Cal., Inc. v. Oxford Nanopore Techs.) and cross-references; guidance advises drafting claims to clearly distinguish working examples from prophetic ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement and undue experimentation timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified that the relevant time for undue experimentation to enable the full scope of the claims is before the effective filing date (discussion referencing Amgen Inc. v. Sanofi and other cases). Changed wording throughout to use 'relevant time' instead of 'time of the invention' or 'date of invention.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added case citations and discussion about undue experimentation and enablement, stressed that the relevant time is the effective filing date (pre-AIA/AIA differences noted), and included cross-references to related MPEP sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction during prosecution (broadest reasonable interpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised text to make it clear that during prosecution the Office construes claims by giving them their broadest reasonable interpretation consistent with the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrected citations (e.g., Nautilus) and clarified that BRI applies during prosecution; includes cross-references to 35 U.S.C. 112(b) guidance and related sections on claim definiteness and rejections under 112.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-sale bar and sale/offer as prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified guidance when a sale or offer for sale may be applied as prior art and may prevent applicant from obtaining a patent. Clarified that the statutory on-sale bar is under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b) and explained applicability to AIA vs pre-AIA contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updated examples, added case citations (including Helsinn), and revised Editor Notes to state applicability to AIA/non-AIA analyses and to avoid impermissible hindsight; cross-references to related sections are added.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of legal precedent in rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised the first paragraph to clarify when and how examiners may use legal precedent as supporting rationale in rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that examiners must support rejections with facts and reasoning, explains limits and proper use of precedent, and adds/updates citations to relevant decisions (e.g., Ahlert). The guidance reminds examiners that reliance on precedent must be contextualized and factual.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) procedural statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Added clarification that a statement under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) is required regardless of any assignment information recorded, and guidance that when the 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) exception applies, the disclosure cannot be applied as a secondary reference in a nonstatutory double patenting rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains procedural requirements for submitting statements under the statutory exception, and implications for double patenting analyses and rejections; included examples and form paragraph revisions.
